# Tokyo Family Trip Plan: 6 Nights, Aug 3–9, 2026

A family-friendly Tokyo plan that keeps hotel changes to a minimum, uses easy train/subway routes, and balances museums, simple meals, and one big theme-park-style day. I’m assuming you’ll stay in one base near a major JR/subway hub such as **Ueno, Tokyo Station, Shinjuku, or Asakusa**.

# Day-by-Day Tokyo Itinerary

## Day 1: Aug 3 — Easy Arrival + Ueno/Asakusa
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and keep the first half-day light; if you land early, do a short reset walk only.
- Afternoon: **Ueno Park** for open space, then **Tokyo National Museum** if everyone has energy; otherwise choose just one museum building.
- Dinner: **Ueno** casual tonkatsu, curry rice, or udon shops with kid-size portions and predictable flavors.
- Transit note: Best as a low-movement first day; Ueno and Asakusa are easy from many central hotels.

## Day 2: Aug 4 — Ueno Museums + Ameyoko + Akihabara
- Morning: **Tokyo National Museum** or **National Museum of Nature and Science**; both work well for children if you keep the visit to 2–3 hours.
- Afternoon: Walk **Ameyoko** for snacks, then continue to **Akihabara** for a short, high-energy stop with arcade time.
- Dinner: **Akihabara/Ueno** family-friendly ramen, curry, or kaiten-style sushi with simple options.
- Transit note: This is an easy rail day with short hops and lots of rest stops.

## Day 3: Aug 5 — Odaiba: Science, Waterfront, and Indoor Fun
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Head to **Odaiba** for **Miraikan** or another hands-on science stop; this is a strong museum day for kids.
- Afternoon: Free time at **DiverCity Tokyo Plaza** or the waterfront; keep it flexible for weather and energy.
- Dinner: **Odaiba** food court or casual family restaurant so picky eaters can choose separately.
- Transit note: Odaiba is very transit-friendly but can feel long if you stack too many stops, so keep it to one main indoor attraction.

## Day 4: Aug 6 — Theme-Park Style Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/ticket-perforated.svg
- Morning: Full day at **Tokyo Disneyland** or **Tokyo DisneySea**; for ages 6 and 10, Disneyland is usually the easier all-around pick.
- Afternoon: Stay in the park and prioritize 3–5 rides plus parade/show time rather than trying to “do everything.”
- Dinner: Eat inside the park or at **Maihama** after exit for a simpler end to the day.
- Transit note: This is the only big-effort day, so plan an early start and a quiet evening.

## Day 5: Aug 7 — Shibuya + Harajuku + Kid-Friendly Shopping
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: **Shibuya Sky** only if you want a view; otherwise start with the **Shibuya Scramble** area and a short department store browse.
- Afternoon: Move to **Harajuku** for **Yoyogi Park** time and a gentle walk on Takeshita Street; keep shopping brief to avoid overload.
- Dinner: **Shibuya/Harajuku** omurice, hamburg steak, or family diner-style meals.
- Transit note: This is a compact neighborhood day with easy walking and short subway rides.

## Day 6: Aug 8 — Kid-Friendly Science or Railway Day + Final Shopping
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Choose one:
  - **Railway Museum** if your kids like trains
  - **National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation** if you want another strong museum option
- Afternoon: Return to central Tokyo for souvenirs, convenience-store snacks, and a final relaxed neighborhood stroll.
- Dinner: **Tokyo Station** or your hotel area for a dependable last-night meal with multiple kid-safe choices.
- Transit note: Keep this day modular so you can adjust based on fatigue and weather.

## Day 7: Aug 9 — Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Pack, check out, and keep breakfast simple near the hotel or station.
- Afternoon: If your flight is late, do a very short station-area stop only; avoid anything that risks rushing.
- Dinner: Usually not needed unless you have a late departure.
- Transit note: Use the most direct airport route from your hotel base; avoid transfers with luggage if possible.

# Budget Fit for ¥280,000 Total

## Practical Spend Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg
- Hotel: **¥120,000–¥160,000** for 6 nights in a family room or two connected rooms in a midrange, transit-friendly area.
- Food: **¥60,000–¥80,000** for 4 people using casual restaurants, food courts, and convenience breakfasts.
- Local transit: **¥12,000–¥20,000** depending on airport transfer choice and how often you use trains.
- Tickets/activities: **¥35,000–¥55,000** depending on museum entries and the theme park choice.
- Buffer: **¥15,000–¥25,000** for snacks, drinks, and small surprises.

## Best Neighborhood Base for Minimal Hotel Changes
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Ueno**: Best overall for museums, easy rail access, and straightforward food.
- **Asakusa**: Good for a calmer family feel and simple sightseeing.
- **Tokyo Station/Marunouchi**: Best if you want the easiest airport and intercity connections.
- **Shinjuku**: Strong transport, but busier and less relaxed with kids than Ueno/Asakusa.

# Transit-Friendly Pacing for Kids

## Daily Rhythm That Usually Works
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- Start late enough to avoid a rushed breakfast.
- Aim for **one main attraction + one easy add-on** per day.
- Build in a snack break every 2–3 hours.
- Use taxis only for short “save the day” hops if kids are tired.
- Keep dinners near the day’s last stop to reduce end-of-day transfers.

# Quick Actions

# Useful Trip Sources

- Tokyo Disney Resort official site: https://www.tokyodisneyresort.jp/en/
- Tokyo Metro route and service info: https://www.tokyometro.jp/en/
- Japan National Tourism Organization Tokyo guide: https://www.japan.travel/en/destinations/kanto/tokyo/
